words.enDefinition: music performed in front of listeners as they hear it

examples.en: The café had live music on Fridays, so we stayed after our usual coffee.
examples.zh: 那家咖啡馆周五有「现场音乐」，所以照常喝完咖啡后，我们又待了一会儿。

examples.en: I could hear live music from the square while walking back to my residence.
examples.zh: 我走回宿舍时，能听见广场传来「现场音乐」。

words.enDefinition: an informal word for a live performance by a musician or band

examples.en: My flatmate played a gig at the student bar after our project ended.
examples.zh: 项目结束后，室友在学生酒吧做了「一场现场演出」。

examples.en: We caught a small gig near the main campus on our way home.
examples.zh: 回家路上，我们在主校区附近看了「一场小型现场演出」。

words.enDefinition: a building or large room designed for musical performances

examples.en: We walked to the concert hall after meeting our classmates at the station.
examples.zh: 我们在车站和同学碰头后，步行去了「音乐厅」。

examples.en: The concert hall was much quieter than the festival stage across the street.
examples.zh: 「音乐厅」比街对面节庆活动的舞台安静得多。

words.enDefinition: a place where musicians perform in front of an audience

examples.en: I had never been to the music venue hidden behind the campus bookshop.
examples.zh: 我以前没去过藏在校园书店后面的那个「音乐演出场地」。

examples.en: A friend showed me the nearest music venue while we were exploring downtown.
examples.zh: 我们逛市中心时，朋友给我指了最近的「音乐演出场地」。

words.enDefinition: a small performance space where the audience feels close to the performers

examples.en: The band chose an intimate venue where we could see the performers clearly.
examples.zh: 乐队选了一个「小型近距离演出场地」，我们能清楚看到表演者。

examples.en: I preferred the intimate venue to the large arena where they had played before.
examples.zh: 比起他们以前演出过的大型场馆，我更喜欢这个「小型近距离演出场地」。

collocations: an intimate venue for live music

words.enDefinition: a designated area where people can dance at a venue

examples.en: My friends went onto the dance floor after the drummer started the next song.
examples.zh: 鼓手开始演奏下一首歌后，我的朋友们走进了「舞池」。

examples.en: I stayed near the dance floor so my flatmate could find me between sets.
examples.zh: 我留在「舞池」旁边，好让室友在两轮演出的间隙找到我。

words.enDefinition: a performer's ability to hold an audience's attention on stage

examples.en: Our friend had great stage presence even though it was her first solo show.
examples.zh: 虽然是第一次独唱演出，朋友的「舞台表现力」已经很强。

examples.en: The tutor asked what gave the singer such strong stage presence during the final song.
examples.zh: 导师问，这位歌手在最后一首歌里为什么会有那么强的「舞台表现力」。

words.enDefinition: the left side of the stage from the position of a performer facing the audience

examples.en: The singer entered from stage left as the lights came up after the break.
examples.zh: 休息过后舞台灯亮了，歌手从「演员视角的舞台左侧」上场。

examples.en: The guitarist waited at stage left until the rest of the band was ready.
examples.zh: 吉他手在「演员视角的舞台左侧」等乐队其他成员准备好。

words.enDefinition: the right side of the stage from the position of a performer facing the audience

examples.en: The keyboard stayed at stage right while the first performer sang by herself.
examples.zh: 第一位表演者独唱时，键盘放在「演员视角的舞台右侧」。

examples.en: The host pointed to stage right and introduced the student players from the jazz society.
examples.zh: 主持人指向「演员视角的舞台右侧」，介绍了爵士社的学生乐手。

words.enDefinition: the main performer advertised for a show or event

examples.en: The headliner went on later than planned because the earlier set ran long.
examples.zh: 前一组表演延长了，「主打艺人」比计划晚出场。

examples.en: A friend from my course recommended the headliner before we went to the festival.
examples.zh: 我们去节庆演出前，同一门课的朋友推荐了那位「主打艺人」。

words.enDefinition: a performer or group that appears before the main performer

examples.en: We arrived early enough to hear the opening act at the student music night.
examples.zh: 我们很早就到了，赶上听了学生音乐之夜的「开场表演者」。

examples.en: The opening act thanked the sound engineer before starting its last song.
examples.zh: 「开场表演者」唱最后一首歌之前感谢了音响师。

words.enDefinition: a performer given a named guest credit on a recording

examples.en: I recognised the featured artist from a playlist that my flatmate had shared.
examples.zh: 我从室友共享过的一个歌单里认出了这位「特邀合作艺人」。

examples.en: The credits listed a featured artist on the song with the second verse in Spanish.
examples.zh: 那首歌的第二段主歌是西班牙语，曲目署名里列了一位「特邀合作艺人」。

words.enDefinition: a singer invited to perform on a particular track or show

examples.en: The band brought out a guest vocalist for one song near the end.
examples.zh: 乐队快结束演出时，请了一位「客座歌手」唱其中一首歌。

examples.en: A guest vocalist sings the chorus on the recording we heard in class.
examples.zh: 我们课上听过的录音，副歌由一位「客座歌手」演唱。

words.enDefinition: a musician who releases or performs music under their own name

examples.en: She returned as a solo artist after spending two years in a band.
examples.zh: 她在乐队演出了两年，之后以「个人名义表演的艺人」身份重返舞台。

examples.en: The solo artist played several songs on guitar before inviting her friends up.
examples.zh: 那位「个人名义表演的艺人」边弹吉他边唱了几首歌，才请朋友们上台。

collocations: launch a career as a solo artist

words.enDefinition: the singer who performs the main vocal part in a group

examples.en: The lead singer asked everyone to join in when the last chorus came around.
examples.zh: 最后一遍副歌唱到时，「主唱」请所有人一起唱。

examples.en: I knew the new lead singer from our campus music society last year.
examples.zh: 我去年在校园音乐社认识了这位新「主唱」。

words.enDefinition: the performer who leads a band onstage and often interacts with the audience

examples.en: The frontperson told a short story while the others changed their instruments onstage.
examples.zh: 其他人在台上换乐器时，「乐队领衔表演者」讲了个小故事。

examples.en: The new frontperson made the crowd laugh halfway through the opening song last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚唱到开场曲一半，新的「乐队领衔表演者」把观众逗笑了。

words.enDefinition: a guitarist who plays the main melodic lines or solos in a group

examples.en: The lead guitarist played a short solo while the singer stepped off the stage.
examples.zh: 歌手走下舞台时，「主音吉他手」弹了一小段独奏。

examples.en: My sister became the lead guitarist in a band she met at university.
examples.zh: 姐姐成了她在大学认识的一支乐队的「主音吉他手」。

words.enDefinition: a guitarist who mainly plays chords or rhythmic parts to support a song

examples.en: The rhythm guitarist kept playing quietly while the singer spoke to the audience.
examples.zh: 歌手和观众说话时，「节奏吉他手」继续轻声伴奏。

examples.en: Our rhythm guitarist suggested a slower pattern when we rehearsed the second number.
examples.zh: 排练第二首歌时，我们的「节奏吉他手」建议把节奏型放慢。

words.enDefinition: a musician who plays a bass instrument, often bass guitar

examples.en: The bass player changed the groove when the crowd began to dance.
examples.zh: 观众开始跳舞时，「贝斯手」改变了演奏的律动。

examples.en: Our new bass player used to perform in the university jazz group last year.
examples.zh: 我们的新「贝斯手」以前在大学爵士乐团演出。

words.enDefinition: singing that supports or complements the main singer's voice

examples.en: Two students sang backing vocals while their classmate sang the lead part onstage.
examples.zh: 同学在台上主唱，另外两名学生负责「伴唱」。

examples.en: I could hear the backing vocals more clearly on the new recording that afternoon.
examples.zh: 那天下午听新录音时，我能更清楚地听见「伴唱」。

words.enDefinition: a musician hired to play for a recording or particular performance

examples.en: A session musician played the piano parts on my friend's first recording at college.
examples.zh: 我朋友在学院第一次录音时，一名「受聘乐手」弹了钢琴声部。

examples.en: Our tutor had worked as a session musician before coming back to teach.
examples.zh: 导师回来教书前做过「受聘乐手」。

words.enDefinition: a band that performs regularly at a particular venue or on a programme

examples.en: The house band played while everyone waited for the first student singer to arrive.
examples.zh: 大家等第一位学生歌手到场时，「场地常驻乐队」在台上演奏。

examples.en: I recognised the guitarist from the house band when I went back a week later.
examples.zh: 一周后再去时，我认出了「场地常驻乐队」的吉他手。

words.enDefinition: a band whose performances center on songs previously performed by other artists

examples.en: A cover band played familiar songs at the outdoor student reception that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚的学生户外招待会上，「翻唱乐队」演唱了大家熟悉的歌。

examples.en: I joined a cover band with three classmates after our first year at university.
examples.zh: 读完大一后，我和三位同学加入了一支「翻唱乐队」。

words.enDefinition: a group that performs in the style of a particular artist or band

examples.en: My friend went to see a tribute band with her father during the holidays.
examples.zh: 假期里，朋友和爸爸一起去看了一支「致敬乐队」。

examples.en: A tribute band performed songs from one group's early recordings all evening last Friday.
examples.zh: 上周五整晚，一支「致敬乐队」都在演出某个乐队早期录制的歌曲。

words.enDefinition: another member of the same band

examples.en: My bandmate suggested that we start with a quieter song at the open rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我的「乐队队友」建议公开排练时，我们先演一首安静一些的歌。

examples.en: An old bandmate came to the café to listen to our new set.
examples.zh: 一位过去的「乐队队友」来咖啡馆听我们新排的一组歌。

words.enDefinition: the performers announced for a particular festival

examples.en: The festival lineup included a group that my flatmate had seen the previous summer.
examples.zh: 「节庆演出阵容」里有一个团队，室友去年夏天看过他们的演出。

examples.en: I checked the festival lineup before asking classmates if they wanted to go on Saturday.
examples.zh: 我先看了「节庆演出阵容」，才问同学们周六想不想去。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled appearance during a tour of performances

examples.en: The band's nearest tour date was the evening before my final university exam.
examples.zh: 乐队离我最近的「巡演日期场次」在我大学最后一门考试的前一天晚上。

examples.en: They added a tour date in our city after their first show sold out.
examples.zh: 第一场票卖完后，他们在我们城市加了一场「巡演场次」。

words.enDefinition: travelling to perform in several different places

examples.en: Our classmate was on tour with the local orchestra for most of the summer.
examples.zh: 暑假大部分时间，我们的同学都和本地管弦乐团一起「在巡演中」。

examples.en: The singer wrote two new songs while on tour with her old friends from school.
examples.zh: 歌手和以前上学认识的朋友「在巡演中」写了两首新歌。

words.enDefinition: a test of sound equipment and performance levels before a show

examples.en: The guitarist played two chords during soundcheck before the venue opened to the public that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚场馆开放前，吉他手在「演出前试音」时弹了两个和弦。

examples.en: I heard part of the soundcheck while waiting outside with the other students.
examples.zh: 我和其他学生在外面等时，听见了一部分「演出前试音」。

words.enDefinition: a control console used to combine and adjust separate audio signals

examples.en: The engineer stayed at the mixing desk throughout the student performers' first rehearsal together.
examples.zh: 学生表演者第一次合排时，音响师一直守在「调音台」旁。

examples.en: I watched a volunteer lower the singer's volume at the mixing desk before the show.
examples.zh: 演出前，我看到一个志愿者在「调音台」上调低了歌手的音量。

words.enDefinition: a speaker that lets performers hear themselves or other players onstage

examples.en: The singer asked for a little more piano in her stage monitor before starting.
examples.zh: 唱之前，歌手请把她的「舞台返听音箱」里的钢琴声调大一些。

examples.en: The technician moved the stage monitor away from the edge of the platform.
examples.zh: 音响技术人员把「舞台返听音箱」从台子边挪开了。

words.enDefinition: an earpiece that lets a musician hear a selected mix while performing

examples.en: The drummer took out an in-ear monitor to speak to us before the show.
examples.zh: 演出开始前，鼓手摘下一只「入耳式返听耳机」跟我们说话。

examples.en: One in-ear monitor stopped working just before the band began its rehearsal that night.
examples.zh: 那晚乐队开始排练前，一只「入耳式返听耳机」突然没声音了。

words.enDefinition: a person who sets up, controls, or records sound for performances

examples.en: The sound engineer asked the band to play the loudest part before the doors opened.
examples.zh: 开门前，「音响工程师」请乐队演奏声音最大的那一段。

examples.en: I sat near the sound engineer during our society's outdoor concert that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚我们社团办户外音乐会时，我坐在「音响工程师」附近。

words.enDefinition: a group of songs performed using mainly acoustic instruments

examples.en: The band played an acoustic set in the library courtyard on Friday afternoon.
examples.zh: 周五下午，乐队在图书馆庭院演出了「原声演奏的一组节目」。

examples.en: I liked the quiet acoustic set before the full band came back onstage.
examples.zh: 完整乐队重新上台前，我很喜欢那段安静的「原声演奏节目」。

words.enDefinition: the list of pieces a performer plans to play in a particular order

examples.en: The setlist was taped to the floor beside the guitarist's shoes during the show.
examples.zh: 演出时，「演出曲目单」贴在吉他手脚边的地板上。

examples.en: I checked the setlist after the gig to find the name of the last song.
examples.zh: 演出结束后，我查了「演出曲目单」，想找最后一首歌的名字。

words.enDefinition: the first piece of music in a performer’s set

examples.en: They chose a fast set opener to get the audience moving before the slower songs.
examples.zh: 他们选了一首快歌作「一轮演出的开场曲」，好在慢歌之前让观众动起来。

examples.en: I recognised the set opener from a recording our tutor played in class.
examples.zh: 我从导师课上放过的一段录音里认出了「一轮演出的开场曲」。

words.enDefinition: the final song or piece played during a musical performance

examples.en: The whole band returned to the stage for the closing number after the singer's solo.
examples.zh: 歌手独唱结束后，全乐队回到台上表演「收尾曲目」。

examples.en: We recorded part of the closing number with the performers' permission from the side.
examples.zh: 征得表演者同意后，我们从侧面录了一段「收尾曲目」。

words.enDefinition: an extra performance after the planned end of a show, often requested by applause

examples.en: The band came back for an encore after everyone clapped for several minutes.
examples.zh: 大家鼓掌几分钟后，乐队回来「返场加演」。

examples.en: We stayed for the encore even though the last bus was leaving soon.
examples.zh: 虽然末班车很快就要开了，我们还是留着看完了「返场加演」。

words.enDefinition: a request from a listener asking for a particular song to be performed

examples.en: The singer took a song request from someone sitting beside us that night.
examples.zh: 那晚，歌手接受了坐在我们旁边的一位观众的「点歌请求」。

examples.en: I wrote a song request on a card and left it near the stage.
examples.zh: 我把「点歌请求」写在卡片上，留在了舞台旁。

words.enDefinition: an occasion when people are invited to sing together, often to familiar music

examples.en: The music society hosted a sing-along in the courtyard after the performance had ended.
examples.zh: 演出结束后，音乐社在庭院里办了场「集体跟唱活动」。

examples.en: The chorus became a sing-along as most people in the room knew the words.
examples.zh: 屋里大多数人都会唱，副歌时就出现了「集体跟唱」。

words.enDefinition: an album made from sessions recorded for release rather than at a live concert

examples.en: We compared the first studio album with the recording from the band's university tour.
examples.zh: 我们把第一张「录音室专辑」和乐队大学巡演的录音作了比较。

examples.en: The artist finished her studio album while working at a café near our campus.
examples.zh: 在我们校园附近的咖啡馆打工期间，那位艺人完成了自己的「录音室专辑」。

words.enDefinition: the first album released by a musician or group

examples.en: My tutor asked us to listen to the debut album before our discussion.
examples.zh: 导师请我们在讨论前先听那张「首张专辑」。

examples.en: The debut album included a song written during the band's final year at school.
examples.zh: 「首张专辑」收录了一首乐队在上学最后一学年写的歌。

words.enDefinition: an album containing recordings made during one or more live performances

examples.en: I liked the live album because you could hear the crowd between songs.
examples.zh: 我喜欢那张「现场录音专辑」，两首歌之间能听到观众的声音。

examples.en: The new live album includes recordings from a concert we watched together last summer.
examples.zh: 新的「现场录音专辑」收录了我们去年夏天一起看的那场音乐会的录音。

words.enDefinition: an album whose songs are linked by a theme, story, or idea

examples.en: My flatmate played the concept album from start to finish on the long train ride.
examples.zh: 长途火车上，室友把那张「概念专辑」从头到尾放了一遍。

examples.en: In class we discussed how the last track developed the idea behind the concept album.
examples.zh: 课上我们讨论了最后一首曲子怎样深化「概念专辑」的主题。

words.enDefinition: an album issued as two discs or presented as two album-length parts

examples.en: The used record shop sold a double album in a thick cardboard sleeve.
examples.zh: 二手唱片店出售一张装在厚纸板封套里的「双碟专辑」。

examples.en: The second disc of the double album was mostly recorded during a concert.
examples.zh: 这张「双碟专辑」的第二张碟主要是在一场演唱会上录制的。

words.enDefinition: an album collecting previously separate recordings by one artist or several artists

examples.en: The campus radio played a track from a compilation album of local performers.
examples.zh: 校园电台播放了一张本地表演者「合辑」里的曲目。

examples.en: I found the song on a compilation album while browsing the used record shop.
examples.zh: 我逛二手唱片店时，在一张「合辑」上找到了这首歌。

words.enDefinition: a collection of an artist's most successful or best-known recordings

examples.en: My host family played a greatest hits album on nearly every drive into town.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭几乎每次开车进城都播放一张「热门作品精选专辑」。

examples.en: The greatest hits album was the first record from the band that I bought.
examples.zh: 我买这支乐队的第一张唱片就是「热门作品精选专辑」。

collocations: tracks on a greatest hits album

words.enDefinition: an album of music associated with a film, show, or similar production

examples.en: I saved the soundtrack album after watching the film at the campus cinema.
examples.zh: 在校园电影院看完电影后，我收藏了「原声音乐专辑」。

examples.en: The soundtrack album had several pieces that only appeared briefly in the film.
examples.zh: 「原声音乐专辑」里有几首曲子在电影中只短暂出现过。

words.enDefinition: a recording of songs from a stage musical performed by a particular cast

examples.en: I borrowed a cast recording after we discussed the musical in our seminar.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论那部音乐剧之后，我借来了一张「音乐剧演员版录音」。

examples.en: The cast recording featured a singer who later gave a talk at our university.
examples.zh: 「音乐剧演员版录音」中有一位歌手，后来到我们学校做过讲座。

words.enDefinition: the act or occasion of making an album publicly available

examples.en: The band planned a small acoustic set to mark its album release that evening.
examples.zh: 乐队计划那晚演一小组原声歌曲，纪念「专辑发行」。

examples.en: My classmate made a poster announcing the album release for his friends' music project.
examples.zh: 同学为朋友的音乐项目做了一张「专辑发行」海报。

words.enDefinition: a gathering in person or online to hear a recording together

examples.en: We had a listening party for our friend's new album in the common room.
examples.zh: 我们在公共休息室为朋友的新专辑办了一场「集体听歌会」。

examples.en: The record store held a listening party before the new album went on sale.
examples.zh: 新专辑开卖前，唱片店举行了「集体听歌会」。

words.enDefinition: the first song released to promote an upcoming album or other collection

examples.en: The duo performed its lead single before talking about the rest of the album.
examples.zh: 两人组合先演了「专辑主打先行单曲」，然后才聊到专辑的其他歌。

examples.en: I recognised the lead single after hearing it on our university radio station.
examples.zh: 在我们学校的电台里听过之后，我认出了「专辑主打先行单曲」。

words.enDefinition: an extended-play music release generally shorter than a full-length album

examples.en: The student band recorded an EP with four songs during the winter break.
examples.zh: 学生乐队寒假录制了一张有四首歌的「迷你专辑」。

examples.en: I bought the EP at the gig after hearing the last song performed live.
examples.zh: 在演出现场听过最后一首歌后，我买了那张「迷你专辑」。

words.enDefinition: a long-playing vinyl record, usually containing a full-length album

examples.en: The record shop played an LP from its used section on a small turntable.
examples.zh: 唱片店用一台小唱机播放二手区的一张「密纹唱片」。

examples.en: I found the LP in a plain sleeve next to two older jazz recordings.
examples.zh: 我在两张较老的爵士录音旁找到了那张装在素色封套里的「密纹唱片」。

words.enDefinition: a track added beyond the main sequence on a particular edition of a release

examples.en: The digital edition included a bonus track from the band's first rehearsal at college.
examples.zh: 数字版附了一首乐队在学院第一次排练时录下的「额外收录曲目」。

examples.en: I bought the new edition because I had never heard the bonus track before.
examples.zh: 我以前没听过「额外收录曲目」，所以买了新版。

words.enDefinition: an unlisted recording placed within or after the apparent end of a release

examples.en: We discovered a hidden track after letting the final song play past the silence.
examples.zh: 我们让最后一首歌继续放过那段静音后，发现了一首「未标出的隐藏曲目」。

examples.en: My friend told me to wait for the hidden track on the older disc.
examples.zh: 朋友让我等一等旧碟上的「未标出的隐藏曲目」。

words.enDefinition: a track with the same name as its album, film, or other work

examples.en: The title track sounded very different when the band played it without drums.
examples.zh: 乐队不加鼓演奏时，「与专辑同名的曲目」听起来很不一样。

examples.en: We started with the title track before playing the rest of the album.
examples.zh: 我们从「与专辑同名的曲目」开始听，之后才放剩下的歌。

words.enDefinition: the first recorded piece in the sequence on an album or other release

examples.en: The opening track began quietly enough that I turned up my headphones that morning.
examples.zh: 那天早上，「开篇曲目」开头很轻，我就把耳机音量调大了。

examples.en: I remembered the opening track from a playlist my classmates made during our trip.
examples.zh: 我记得「开篇曲目」曾出现在同学们出游时做的歌单里。

words.enDefinition: a short piece of music between longer songs or sections

examples.en: The piano interlude gave everyone time to settle back into their seats.
examples.zh: 那段钢琴「间奏小段」让大家有时间重新坐好。

examples.en: There was a quiet interlude between the two loud tracks on the album.
examples.zh: 专辑里两首很响的曲子之间有一个安静的「间奏小段」。

words.enDefinition: a recorded track performed with instruments and without sung words

examples.en: I added an instrumental track to the playlist I use for writing essays.
examples.zh: 我在写论文听的歌单里加了一首「无唱词的器乐曲目」。

examples.en: The final instrumental track used the same melody as the album's first song.
examples.zh: 最后一首「无唱词的器乐曲目」用了和专辑第一首歌相同的旋律。

words.enDefinition: the less-promoted side of a single record or a track associated with that side

examples.en: My uncle played the B-side after showing me the label on the old single.
examples.zh: 叔叔给我看了旧单曲唱片的标签后，放了「单曲唱片反面曲目」。

examples.en: The band's B-side later became more popular than the song promoted at first.
examples.zh: 乐队的「单曲唱片反面曲目」后来比最开始推广的那首歌还火。

words.enDefinition: the ordered list of pieces in a particular recording or release

examples.en: I checked the tracklist to find which song played after the piano piece.
examples.zh: 我查看「专辑曲目清单」，想找钢琴曲后面放的是哪首歌。

examples.en: The band changed the tracklist slightly before making the album available to listeners.
examples.zh: 专辑向听众上线前，乐队稍微调整了「专辑曲目清单」。

words.enDefinition: written information included with a record or album about the works and contributors

examples.en: I read the liner notes to find out who had played the piano.
examples.zh: 我读了「唱片内页说明」，想知道钢琴是谁弹的。

examples.en: The liner notes included a short story about how the band found its drummer.
examples.zh: 「唱片内页说明」里有个小故事，讲乐队是怎么找到鼓手的。

words.enDefinition: the images and design associated with the packaging or display of an album

examples.en: My classmate designed the album artwork for a student band in her spare time.
examples.zh: 同学用业余时间给一支学生乐队做了「专辑视觉设计」。

examples.en: The album artwork was based on a photograph taken behind the old music building.
examples.zh: 「专辑视觉设计」以旧音乐楼后面拍的一张照片为基础。

words.enDefinition: a protective paper or cardboard cover that holds a vinyl record

examples.en: The record sleeve was worn at the corners, but the disc still looked clean.
examples.zh: 「唱片封套」的角磨损了，不过唱片看着还很干净。

examples.en: I put the disc back in its record sleeve before passing it to my flatmate.
examples.zh: 递给室友之前，我把碟放回了「唱片封套」里。

collocations: put a disc in its record sleeve

words.enDefinition: a release of music that had already been made available at an earlier time

examples.en: The new reissue included photos from the original recording sessions in the university studio.
examples.zh: 新的「再版发行」收录了当年在大学录音室录制时的照片。

examples.en: I bought the reissue because the older copy was difficult to find locally.
examples.zh: 旧版在当地难找，我就买了「再版」。

words.enDefinition: to prepare a new master recording from existing material to improve or change its sound

examples.en: The label decided to remaster the live recording before putting it online last year.
examples.zh: 唱片公司去年把现场录音放到网上之前，决定「重新处理母带」。

examples.en: A graduate from our course helped remaster the tracks from the band's early sessions.
examples.zh: 我们专业的一位毕业生帮忙为乐队早期录制的曲目「重新处理母带」。

words.enDefinition: an expanded edition of a release that usually contains additional material

examples.en: The deluxe edition came with demos that the band recorded during its final year.
examples.zh: 「豪华版专辑」附有乐队最后一年录制的几首样带。

examples.en: I compared the deluxe edition with the older one before buying the record.
examples.zh: 我买唱片前，先比较了「豪华版专辑」和旧版。

words.enDefinition: an early recording made to demonstrate how a song or arrangement might sound

examples.en: My friend played me a demo recording she had made in her bedroom.
examples.zh: 朋友给我放了她在卧室录的一段「歌曲示范录音」。

examples.en: The band changed the chorus after listening to the demo recording from Monday.
examples.zh: 乐队听了周一的「歌曲示范录音」后，改了副歌。

words.enDefinition: a temporary mix made to hear how the recorded elements fit together

examples.en: The tutor listened to our rough mix before suggesting changes to the guitar level.
examples.zh: 导师听了我们的「初步混音」后，建议改动吉他的音量。

examples.en: I saved the rough mix so we could compare it with the final version.
examples.zh: 我保存了「初步混音」，方便和最终版比较。

collocations: listen back to the rough mix

words.enDefinition: a new performance of a piece already recorded or performed by another artist

examples.en: The student band played a cover version of a song we all knew.
examples.zh: 学生乐队演奏了一首大家都知道的歌的「翻唱或翻奏版本」。

examples.en: I heard the cover version before I found the original recording in the library.
examples.zh: 我先听了「翻唱版本」，后来才在图书馆找到原录音。

words.enDefinition: a version of a song performed mainly using acoustic instruments

examples.en: The singer played an acoustic version of the song on a small wooden stage.
examples.zh: 歌手在小木台上演了这首歌的「原声乐器演奏版」。

examples.en: I preferred the acoustic version because I could follow the words more easily.
examples.zh: 我更喜欢「原声乐器演奏版」，那一版的歌词更容易听清。

words.enDefinition: a version of a song shortened or otherwise adapted for radio play

examples.en: The radio edit left out the long introduction that I remembered from the album.
examples.zh: 「广播剪辑版」省掉了我记得专辑里有的那段长前奏。

examples.en: The station played a radio edit before the programme moved on to local news.
examples.zh: 电台放了一个「广播剪辑版」，之后节目转入本地新闻。

words.enDefinition: a version of a song with explicit language or content removed or replaced

examples.en: The teacher selected the clean version when she played the track in class.
examples.zh: 老师在课上放那首歌时，选了「删除不雅词语的版本」。

examples.en: I found the clean version in the playlist supplied by the campus radio team.
examples.zh: 我在校园电台团队提供的歌单里找到了「删除不雅词语的版本」。

words.enDefinition: a longer mix of a song, often with more repeated beats or instrumental sections

examples.en: The DJ used an extended mix while people were beginning to fill the dance floor.
examples.zh: 大家陆续走进舞池时，DJ 放的是「加长混音版」。

examples.en: We noticed that the extended mix began with a much longer drum pattern than usual.
examples.zh: 我们注意到，「加长混音版」一开头的鼓点比普通版长得多。

words.enDefinition: a different version of recorded music made by changing or recombining its sounds

examples.en: I liked the remix because it brought the quiet backing vocals forward a little.
examples.zh: 我喜欢「重新混音版」，这一版把原本很轻的伴唱调得稍突出些。

examples.en: The DJ played a remix with a quicker beat near the end of the set.
examples.zh: DJ 的表演快结束时，放了一个节奏更快的「重新混音版」。

words.enDefinition: a track made by combining recognisable parts of two or more recordings

examples.en: Our music tutor played a mashup that used vocals and drums from different songs.
examples.zh: 音乐导师播放了一首「混搭歌曲」，其中人声和鼓来自不同的歌。

examples.en: I recognised the older tune immediately when it appeared in the student DJ's mashup.
examples.zh: 学生 DJ 的「混搭歌曲」一放出那段老旋律，我立刻就认出来了。

words.enDefinition: a musical performance connecting parts of several songs in one continuous sequence

examples.en: The choir ended the show with a medley of songs from old musicals.
examples.zh: 合唱团用几部老音乐剧里的歌曲组成「串烧曲目」，结束了演出。

examples.en: We rehearsed the medley slowly to make each change between songs feel natural.
examples.zh: 我们慢慢排练「串烧曲目」，让每次换歌都显得自然。

words.zhGloss: 采入新作品的一段录音
words.enDefinition: a short section of an existing recording used within a new piece of music
acceptedZhAnswers: 采入新作品的一段录音

examples.en: The producer used a music sample from a drum recording made by her classmate.
examples.zh: 制作人使用了一段同学录制的鼓乐作为「采入新作品的录音」。

examples.en: I recognised the music sample from a record we had listened to in class.
examples.zh: 我认出了这段「采入新作品的录音」，它来自我们在课上听过的唱片。

words.enDefinition: a person who writes music or words for songs

examples.en: A songwriter from the university performed several of his own pieces at the café.
examples.zh: 一位校内「歌曲创作者」在咖啡馆演唱了几首自己的作品。

examples.en: The songwriter told us that the melody came first and the words much later.
examples.zh: 「歌曲创作者」告诉我们，先有旋律，很久之后才写歌词。

words.enDefinition: someone whose role is to write the words for songs

examples.en: The lyricist changed the last line after hearing the singers rehearse together that morning.
examples.zh: 那天上午听歌手们合排后，「歌词作者」改了最后一句词。

examples.en: Our programme introduced the lyricist separately from the composer of the music that evening.
examples.zh: 当晚节目单把「歌词作者」与作曲者分别介绍。

words.enDefinition: a person who guides the making and creative sound of a recording

examples.en: The record producer suggested recording the piano separately in the smaller room.
examples.zh: 「唱片制作人」建议把钢琴声部放到较小的房间单独录制。

examples.en: My tutor had worked as a record producer before joining the music department.
examples.zh: 导师进入音乐系工作前做过「唱片制作人」。

words.enDefinition: a music video that displays the words of the song as it plays

examples.en: I watched the lyric video to check one line I had always misheard.
examples.zh: 我看了「歌词视频」，确认一句自己一直听错的歌词。

examples.en: The band released a simple lyric video featuring drawings made by local students.
examples.zh: 乐队发布了一个简单的「歌词视频」，配上当地学生画的图。

words.enDefinition: the first verse of a song

examples.en: She sang the opening verse alone before the other students joined the chorus.
examples.zh: 她先自己唱了「第一段主歌」，其他同学到副歌才加进来。

examples.en: I knew the opening verse even though I couldn't remember the rest of the words.
examples.zh: 虽然记不得其他歌词，我还是会唱「第一段主歌」。

words.enDefinition: the recurring main section that usually follows a verse

examples.en: Our friends could sing the chorus of the song before learning the verses.
examples.zh: 朋友们还没学会各段主歌，就已经能唱「歌曲副歌」了。

examples.en: I recognised the chorus of the song after hearing just a few notes.
examples.zh: 只听到几个音，我就认出了「歌曲副歌」。

collocations: sing the chorus of the song
repeat the chorus of the song
learn the chorus of the song

words.enDefinition: a contrasting section connecting or separating familiar parts of a song

examples.en: The bridge section changed key before the band went back to the familiar chorus.
examples.zh: 乐队回到熟悉的副歌之前，「歌曲的过渡段」转了调。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the bridge section felt calmer than the rest of the song.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么「歌曲的过渡段」比其他部分听起来更平静。

words.enDefinition: a memorable piece of melody that catches the listener's attention

examples.en: I could hum the melodic hook by the time the second chorus came around.
examples.zh: 唱到第二遍副歌时，我已经能哼出那段「抓耳旋律片段」了。

examples.en: We changed the backing arrangement but kept the melodic hook from the first draft.
examples.zh: 我们调整了伴奏编排，保留了第一稿的「抓耳旋律片段」。

words.enDefinition: a short pattern of notes played repeatedly on a guitar within a piece

examples.en: The opening guitar riff reminded me of a song we heard on campus radio.
examples.zh: 开头的「吉他重复短乐句」让我想起了校园电台放过一首歌。

examples.en: My classmate played the guitar riff slowly so I could work out the rhythm.
examples.zh: 同学把「吉他重复短乐句」弹慢一些，让我能弄清节奏。

words.enDefinition: the series of low notes forming the bass part of a piece

examples.en: The new bassline gave the slow song a rhythm that people could dance to.
examples.zh: 新的「低音声部旋律线」给这首慢歌加上了可以跳舞的节奏。

examples.en: We noticed the bassline most clearly after the drummer paused for a moment.
examples.zh: 鼓手暂时停下一会儿后，「低音声部旋律线」听得最清楚。

words.enDefinition: a short variation on the main drum pattern between sections of music

examples.en: I heard a drum fill just before the singer came back in that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚歌手重新唱起来之前，我听到一个「鼓点过门」。

examples.en: The drummer practised the drum fill that linked the slower verse to the chorus.
examples.zh: 鼓手练习了把较慢的主歌和副歌连起来的「鼓点过门」。

words.enDefinition: a moment when the full beat or bass enters strongly after a musical buildup

examples.en: The beat drop near the end brought the crowd back onto the dance floor.
examples.zh: 快结束时的「节拍骤入」让观众又回到了舞池。

examples.en: We could hear the beat drop from the hallway as we waited to go inside.
examples.zh: 我们在走廊等着进去，隔着墙也听见了「节拍骤入」。

words.enDefinition: a melody that is easy to remember and likely to stay in your mind

examples.en: The film used a catchy tune that we hummed all the way home.
examples.zh: 电影用了一段「好记上口的曲调」，我们一路哼着回家。

examples.en: My friend wrote a catchy tune for the university's short video last spring.
examples.zh: 去年春天，朋友为学校的短视频写了一段「好记上口的曲调」。

words.enDefinition: a slow emotional pop or rock song that builds to a strong, dramatic sound

examples.en: The band saved its power ballad for the moment when the lights came up.
examples.zh: 乐队把那首「强劲抒情歌曲」留到灯光亮起时演奏。

examples.en: My roommate sang the power ballad so loudly that we heard it downstairs.
examples.zh: 室友唱那首「强劲抒情歌曲」很大声，我们在楼下都听到了。

words.enDefinition: a song or tune that keeps repeating in your mind without effort

examples.en: The short theme from the video became an earworm while I was studying.
examples.zh: 视频的简短主题曲成了我学习时「在脑子里循环的曲子」。

examples.en: The chorus became an earworm after the gig, and I hummed it for days.
examples.zh: 演出后，那段副歌成了我「在脑子里循环的曲子」，我哼了好几天。

words.enDefinition: a phrase used when a tune or thought keeps repeating in your mind

examples.en: That chorus was stuck in my head all afternoon while I worked in the library.
examples.zh: 我下午在图书馆干活时，那段副歌一直「在我脑海里挥之不去」。

examples.en: The song from our performance is still stuck in my head from last night.
examples.zh: 我们昨晚演的那首歌现在还「在我脑海里挥之不去」。

words.enDefinition: to sing at the correct pitches for the music

examples.en: It was easier to sing in tune once I could hear the piano clearly.
examples.zh: 能听清伴奏钢琴后，我更容易「唱得不跑调」。

examples.en: Our friend helped us sing in tune by playing the first notes before rehearsal.
examples.zh: 排练前，朋友弹了开头几个音，帮我们「唱得不跑调」。

collocations: be able to sing in tune

words.enDefinition: not matching the right pitch or key when singing or playing

examples.en: I was slightly off-key until the guitarist played the right starting note again.
examples.zh: 吉他手再次弹出正确的起音前，我唱得有点「音高不准」。

examples.en: The tutor stopped us when the last note sounded off-key during rehearsal on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二排练时，最后一个音听起来「音高不准」，导师叫停了我们。

words.enDefinition: to maintain or follow the pulse of a piece of music

examples.en: I tried to keep time by listening to the drummer instead of watching the lights.
examples.zh: 我尽量听鼓手来「合着节拍」，不去看灯光。

examples.en: The piano helped us keep time while the singers learned the new arrangement.
examples.zh: 歌手学新编排时，钢琴帮我们「合着节拍」。

words.enDefinition: to make small rhythmic taps while listening to a piece of music

examples.en: I began to tap along when the band played a tune I knew.
examples.zh: 乐队演奏一首我认识的曲子时，我开始「跟着节奏轻打拍子」。

examples.en: My cousin couldn't help but tap along quietly at the back of the room.
examples.zh: 表亲在屋后忍不住「跟着节奏轻轻打拍子」。

words.enDefinition: to reproduce music by listening rather than reading written notes

examples.en: My roommate can play by ear after listening to a melody a few times.
examples.zh: 室友听几遍旋律后，就能「凭听觉演奏」。

examples.en: I tried to play by ear when we couldn't find the sheet music online.
examples.zh: 网上找不到乐谱时，我试着「凭听觉演奏」。

collocations: be able to play by ear

words.enDefinition: to read and perform a piece from its score without preparing it in advance

examples.en: We had to sight-read music for a short exercise in the campus choir rehearsal.
examples.zh: 校园合唱团排练时有项简短练习，需要我们「视谱演唱」。

examples.en: My classmate can sight-read music on piano much faster than I can these days.
examples.zh: 最近我同学用钢琴「视谱演奏」比我快得多。

words.enDefinition: a recording prepared for someone to sing along to without the original lead vocal

examples.en: We tried the karaoke track once before asking everyone else to join us.
examples.zh: 我们先试唱了一遍「卡拉 OK 伴奏曲」，才请其他人加入。

examples.en: I chose a karaoke track that started with a simple piano introduction that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚我选了一首以简单钢琴前奏开场的「卡拉 OK 伴奏曲」。

collocations: sing along to a karaoke track

words.enDefinition: an informal get-together where musicians play together, often without a fixed arrangement

examples.en: I brought my guitar to the jam session after finishing my last class.
examples.zh: 上完最后一节课后，我带吉他去了「即兴合奏活动」。

examples.en: Our jam session became quieter once we moved from the courtyard into the common room.
examples.zh: 我们从庭院移到公共休息室后，「即兴合奏活动」安静了一些。

words.enDefinition: printed or digital notation showing how a piece should be played or sung

examples.en: I left the sheet music on the piano after working through the second page.
examples.zh: 练完第二页后，我把「乐谱」留在钢琴上。

examples.en: My tutor emailed the sheet music before we chose a time for our first rehearsal.
examples.zh: 我们选定第一次排练的时间之前，导师发来了「乐谱」。

words.enDefinition: a book containing the words, musical notation, or both for a set of songs

examples.en: The library's songbook included a shorter version of the piece we were learning.
examples.zh: 图书馆那本「歌曲集」里有我们在学的曲子的简短版。

examples.en: I borrowed a songbook from my roommate before going to the student choir rehearsal.
examples.zh: 去学生合唱团排练之前，我向室友借了一本「歌曲集」。

words.enDefinition: a batch or edition of records manufactured on vinyl

examples.en: The shop showed me a vinyl pressing with a different sleeve from the original.
examples.zh: 店家给我看了一个「压制发行的黑胶版本」，封套和最初版不一样。

examples.en: I bought the vinyl pressing after hearing how different it sounded from the streaming version.
examples.zh: 我听出它和流媒体版的声音差别之后，买了「压制发行的黑胶版本」。

words.enDefinition: a store selling recordings, especially vinyl records or CDs

examples.en: I stopped at the record shop before catching the train home after class.
examples.zh: 下课坐火车回家前，我去了趟「唱片店」。

examples.en: The small record shop hosted a listening party for a local artist that evening.
examples.zh: 那晚，这家小「唱片店」为一位本地艺人办了集体听歌会。

words.enDefinition: a person who selects and arranges tracks for a playlist

examples.en: Our campus radio playlist curator picked songs by several musicians from the university.
examples.zh: 我们校园电台的「歌单策划人」选了几位校内音乐人的歌。

examples.en: A playlist curator asked our band to suggest a song for the evening programme.
examples.zh: 一位「歌单策划人」请我们乐队为晚间节目推荐一首歌。

words.enDefinition: a playback mode that plays tracks in a different order from the displayed list

examples.en: I switched to shuffle play after hearing the first few tracks in order.
examples.zh: 按顺序听过开头几首后，我切到了「随机顺序播放」。

examples.en: The app returned to shuffle play when I reopened it on the bus.
examples.zh: 我在公交上重新打开音乐应用时，应用回到了「随机顺序播放」。

words.enDefinition: to choose to play a song or list over and over

examples.en: There was one track I wanted to put on repeat while working on the poster.
examples.zh: 做海报时，有一首我想「设置循环播放」。

examples.en: I asked which song we should put on repeat for the walk home that evening.
examples.zh: 我问那晚走回家时，该把哪首歌「设置循环播放」。

collocations: choose a song to put on repeat
decide what to put on repeat

words.enDefinition: the list of songs or other items scheduled to play next

examples.en: I reordered the playback queue before the rest of the housemates came home.
examples.zh: 其他室友回家之前，我重新排了「待播放队列」。

examples.en: The playback queue showed the tracks we had added during lunch in that same order.
examples.zh: 「待播放队列」按同样的顺序显示了我们午饭时添加的曲目。

words.enDefinition: to place a song or other item among those waiting to play next

examples.en: I chose a song to add to the queue instead of interrupting the album.
examples.zh: 我选了一首歌「加入待播队列」，避免打断正在播放的专辑。

examples.en: The app showed which tracks I could add to the queue after selecting the playlist.
examples.zh: 我选了歌单后，应用列出了可以「加入待播队列」的曲目。

collocations: choose tracks to add to the queue
option to add to the queue
select a song to add to the queue

words.enDefinition: a change in which one track fades out while the next fades in

examples.en: The crossfade made the change between the two dance tracks sound much less abrupt.
examples.zh: 「交叉淡入淡出」让两首舞曲之间的切换听起来没那么突兀。

examples.en: I turned off the crossfade to hear the proper ending of the piano piece.
examples.zh: 我关掉了「交叉淡入淡出」，好听清钢琴曲真正的结尾。

words.enDefinition: continuous playback without adding silence between consecutive tracks

examples.en: The recording sounded more natural with gapless playback because the applause never dropped out.
examples.zh: 用「无间隙播放」听这张录音更自然，掌声不会突然中断。

examples.en: My flatmate turned on gapless playback for the album recorded at a single concert.
examples.zh: 室友给那张整场音乐会录下的专辑开了「无间隙播放」。

words.enDefinition: listening to downloaded recordings when an internet connection is unavailable or unused

examples.en: I downloaded the album for offline listening before getting on the long-distance coach.
examples.zh: 上长途大巴前，我下载了专辑，以便「离线收听」。

examples.en: The settings page showed which playlists were available for offline listening that weekend.
examples.zh: 设置页列出了那个周末可「离线收听」的歌单。

words.enDefinition: played very frequently on a station or person's regular listening list

examples.en: The group's first song was on heavy rotation on campus radio all through spring.
examples.zh: 整个春季，这支乐队的第一首歌在校园电台「被高频反复播放」。

examples.en: The album was on heavy rotation in our flat while we prepared for exams.
examples.zh: 准备考试期间，这张专辑在我们的公寓里「被高频反复播放」。

collocations: keep a song on heavy rotation
put a track on heavy rotation

words.enDefinition: rock music associated with independent scenes and a variety of alternative styles

examples.en: We listened to indie rock at the café recommended by our former flatmate.
examples.zh: 我们在老室友推荐的咖啡馆里听了「独立摇滚」。

examples.en: My friend started an indie rock band with classmates from the music department.
examples.zh: 朋友和音乐系的几名同学组了一支「独立摇滚」乐队。

words.enDefinition: music rooted in community traditions or a style based on those traditions

examples.en: The campus event mixed folk music from different regions with stories from the performers.
examples.zh: 校园活动把不同地区的「民间音乐」与表演者讲的故事放到了一起。

examples.en: My roommate grew up hearing folk music at family gatherings in her hometown.
examples.zh: 室友从小在家乡的家庭聚会上听「民间音乐」。

words.enDefinition: music composed for a small group of players, usually with one player to each part

examples.en: We listened to chamber music played by three students in the campus recital room.
examples.zh: 我们在学校的小演奏厅听了三位学生演出的「室内乐」。

examples.en: The music club chose chamber music for the quieter space near the library.
examples.zh: 音乐社为图书馆附近较安静的场所选了「室内乐」。

words.enDefinition: a well-known jazz piece that many performers regularly learn or perform

examples.en: The pianist opened with a jazz standard that several students in the audience recognised.
examples.zh: 钢琴手用一首观众席上好几位学生都认识的「爵士常演经典曲」开场。

examples.en: I learned a jazz standard with two classmates before the evening jam session.
examples.zh: 晚间即兴合奏活动前，我和两位同学学了一首「爵士常演经典曲」。

words.enDefinition: a music tradition developed by African Americans that commonly uses distinctive forms and expressive notes

examples.en: The campus radio show introduced blues alongside short interviews with local guitar players.
examples.zh: 校园电台节目介绍了「布鲁斯音乐」，还放了几段对本地吉他手的简短采访。

examples.en: I started listening to blues after borrowing an old record from my uncle.
examples.zh: 向叔叔借了一张老唱片后，我开始听「布鲁斯音乐」。

words.enDefinition: a musical style within hip-hop culture, commonly using rapped vocals and rhythmic beats

examples.en: The library hosted a discussion about hip-hop and spoken performance that Thursday evening.
examples.zh: 那周四傍晚，图书馆办了一场关于「嘻哈音乐」和口述表演的讨论。

examples.en: My flatmate made a hip-hop playlist for our long bus ride after exams.
examples.zh: 室友为我们考后坐长途公交做了一份「嘻哈音乐」歌单。

words.enDefinition: rhythmic music made primarily with electronic equipment for dancing

examples.en: I heard electronic dance music coming from the student hall as we arrived.
examples.zh: 我们到的时候，听见学生礼堂传出「电子舞曲」。

examples.en: The radio team scheduled electronic dance music for the last hour of its programme.
examples.zh: 电台团队把「电子舞曲」安排在了节目最后一小时。

words.enDefinition: a style of electronic dance music with a steady beat, originating in Chicago

examples.en: The DJ switched to house music after the first group finished its campus performance.
examples.zh: 第一个团队结束校园演出后，DJ 换成了「浩室舞曲」。

examples.en: My classmate lent me an album of house music to try on the train.
examples.zh: 同学借我一张「浩室舞曲」专辑，让我在火车上听听。

words.enDefinition: popular music from South Korea, often associated with its recorded and live pop industry

examples.en: The dance society practised a routine to K-pop in the common room after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，舞蹈社在公共休息室配合「韩国流行音乐」练舞。

examples.en: My roommates shared their favourite K-pop tracks while we cooked dinner for the group.
examples.zh: 我们给大家做晚饭时，室友们分享了最喜欢的「韩国流行音乐」曲目。

words.enDefinition: a broad style of contemporary West African popular music associated especially with Nigeria and Ghana

examples.en: A friend played Afrobeats while we helped move chairs for the student music night.
examples.zh: 我们帮学生音乐之夜搬椅子时，朋友放了「西非流行音乐」。

examples.en: The radio presenter featured Afrobeats tracks chosen by students from several different courses.
examples.zh: 电台主持人重点播放了几门不同专业课程的学生选出的「西非流行音乐」曲目。
